I squashed this and rebased it on #12756. Two conflicts, both from my "Don't look up custom element definitions for sanitized-away elements" commit (fab5f2bc) and this PR independently factoring `sanitize` into an element-name algorithm. Resolved as follows:

- Kept this PR's "sanitizer action for element name" and dropped my "get the sanitizer action for an element name" and the `sanitize` wrapper, since this PR removes that algorithm and moves the `sanitize` dfn to the intro prose.
- In "create an element for a token", merged this PR's steps (switch `document` to the template contents owner for dropped elements, sanitize the `is` attribute) with my step that skips the custom element definition lookup for dropped elements. Both needed the action, so I compute it once into `sanitizerAction` and use it in both places.
- My Noah's Ark note linked to "sanitize attributes", which this PR removes. I repointed it to "create an element for the token" and reworded the rationale, since removed attributes are now never appended to the element rather than removed afterwards.

Otherwise the diff is unchanged from before the rebase.

AI review Reviewed at `bc618bff`, together with wpt#61748 at `6fdd1124`. Chromium's code was compared and Chrome Canary 157 was run by agents; I traced the spec myself. The core write/close/abort, re-entrancy, script timing, sanitizer and Trusted Types paths match Chromium. **Blockers** - *stream HTML* step 3 (`source:127885`) vs wpt `domparsing/stream-html-script-safe.html:39, 71, 98, 113`: for a `script` context, the spec has the *safe* variants return a stream that discards chunks. Chromium (`html_stream.cc:142-147`) and the test (18 subtests) throw `NotSupportedError` instead. Either align the spec with Chromium's throw, or keep the discarding stream and fix the test and Chromium. The discarding stream matches what `setHTML()` does on a `script`. - *Adoption agency algorithm* (`source:149763`, `149976`): pushing one element queue per outer-loop iteration makes custom element callbacks for moved nodes run synchronously in *document* parsing too, where main used the backup element queue. Chromium also runs them synchronously, but once per insertion (`html_construction_site.cc:220`), so callbacks see intermediate trees: for `

` with two elements moved, Chromium gives d1 c1 d2 c2 twice, while the PR gives d1 c1 d1 c1 d2 c2 d2 c2. Consider running reactions around each move to match Chromium, and adding a document-parsing test. This changes behavior beyond streaming, so it should also go in the commit message. **Suggestions** - *Abort a fragment parser* (`source:151841`): Chromium aborts immediately when a `connectedCallback` aborts the stream while the parser runs from a task after a blocking script (`html_stream.cc:92-98`), so the rest of the chunk is dropped. The spec defers the abort. No wpt test reaches the "fragment parser running" or "abort requested" paths, e.g. `w.write('

')`. Consider adding one and filing a Chromium bug. - *Prepare the script element*, force-async note (`source:68516`): the note says `createContextualFragment()` external scripts run in order once inserted. Chromium runs them out of order, for streamed scripts as well as for `createContextualFragment()` and `setHTMLUnsafe()` with `runScripts` (the latter two are pre-existing). There's no test; consider adding one along with a Chromium bug. - `source:148164-148170`: the #12756 note on the declarative shadow root registry says a sanitizing parse's host is always in the inert or `parseHTML()` document, which is null-registry. With streaming into a live document, a kept host is in the live document, and a removed host is in the template contents owner document. The outcome still holds, but the reasoning should be updated. - *parent for HTML streaming* (`source:127852`): `streamBeforeHTML()`/`streamAfterHTML()`/`streamReplaceWithHTML()` throw `"HierarchyRequestError"` for a node without a parent, while `beforeHTML()` and friends silently do nothing. Is the inconsistency intended? - wpt expectations that don't match the spec. All pass in Canary only because they encode Chromium behavior: - `stream-html-defer-async-script.html:31-32, 38-39`: expects a parser-blocking `data:` script to have run when `write()` settles. The write promise doesn't wait, which contradicts `stream-html-parser-blocking-script.html:265, 270`. - `stream-html-stylesheet-does-not-block-scripts.html:85`: I think `#after-external` is still missing after `await writer.close()`. The close runs inside the microtask checkpoint after the external script, while the parser is still paused. - `stream-html-live-document.html:62`: expects `readyState === "complete"` synchronously after `doc.close()`. *The end* only sets "interactive"; Fx Nightly gives "interactive". - wpt `stream-html-with-trusted-types-adopt.html:59-70` and `stream-html-with-trusted-types-from-non-tt.html:45-56` check Trusted Types against the adopted node's *new* document's global. The spec uses `this`'s relevant global object, which doesn't change on adoption, the same as `setHTMLUnsafe()`. Either change the spec for all the Unsafe methods, or keep these files `.tentative`. - wpt tests that pass trivially: - `stream-html-custom-element-sanitizer.html:94, 181` use `attachShadow({registry})` instead of `customElementRegistry`, so the scoped-registry subtests test nothing. - `move-head-during-prepend-before-close-crash.html:7` calls `documentElement.streamPrependHTML()`, which throws per spec, so the crash path is never reached. - `stream-append-html.html:132-147` takes its color from an earlier test's style sheet. Chromium bugs where the tests are right: an `html` target or parent doesn't throw (24 failures in `stream-html-element.html`), and `stream-tokenizer-context.html` takes *parser scripting disabled* from the template contents document.

> AI review

Thanks for the thorough review! Addressed as follows (commits on top of the rebase):

Blockers

- stream HTML step 3: went with aligning the spec with Chromium/wpt — the safe variants now also throw "NotSupportedError" for a script context. Added a note explaining why this deliberately differs from setHTML(): a stream that silently discards everything is an easy mistake to miss, and streaming partial source into a script is never useful. The six safe domintros were updated to match; stream-html-script-safe.html is now consistent with the spec.
 - Adoption agency: this is pre-existing in document parsing and unrelated to streaming, so I'd rather not change the AAA in this PR — I've dropped the per-iteration queue entirely (the AAA is now identical to main) and filed #13072 for the Chromium/spec mismatch. In the same spirit I also removed the run-wide element queue in run a fragment parser (7b8409db7): insertions are already covered by the per-insertion queue (now also for fragment parsers), and anything else goes to the backup element queue and runs at the next microtask checkpoint, exactly as for the document parser. That was the only place where streaming's reaction timing differed from the main parser, and it made chunk boundaries observable.

Suggestions

- Abort a fragment parser: kept the deferral — it's deliberate, to avoid tearing the parser down re-entrantly, consistent with how re-entrant write()/close() are treated. I'll add a test that reaches the "fragment parser running"/"abort requested" paths and file a Chromium bug.
- Force-async note: the note is accurate per spec; Chromium running these out of order is a Chromium bug (pre-existing for createContextualFragment()/setHTMLUnsafe()). Added test and filed a chromium gbug.
DSR registry note: updated the reasoning to cover the live document and its appropriate template contents owner document (50d7b32a9).
- parent for HTML streaming: the throw is intentional — a stream needs to be usable at creation time, and a node detached mid-stream already errors the stream with the same exception. Added a note saying so (50d7b32a9).
wpt mismatches (defer-async-script, stylesheet-does-not-block-scripts, live-document readyState): agreed the spec is right in all three; Tests fixed.
- Trusted Types adopt tests: the spec intentionally matches setHTMLUnsafe() (this's relevant global). I'll keep those files .tentative for now rather than changing all the Unsafe methods here.
- Trivially-passing tests (customElementRegistry option name, html target in the crash test, leaked style in stream-append-html.html): fixed
- Chromium bugs (html target/parent not throwing; parser scripting disabled from the template contents document): filed.

> * Adoption agency: this is pre-existing in document parsing and unrelated to streaming, so I'd rather not change the AAA in this PR — I've dropped the per-iteration queue entirely (the AAA is now identical to main) and filed [Timing of CE reactions with adoption agency #13072](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13072) for the Chromium/spec mismatch. In the same spirit I also removed the run-wide element queue in run a fragment parser ([7b8409d](https://github.com/whatwg/html/commit/7b8409db70afdfc1d09b67438cf92e5a87827eb6)): insertions are already covered by the per-insertion queue (now also for fragment parsers), and anything else goes to the backup element queue and runs at the next microtask checkpoint, exactly as for the document parser. That was the only place where streaming's reaction timing differed from the main parser, and it made chunk boundaries observable.

The push and pop (new steps 14 and 31) should also to be removed to match main.

The reviews brought up a couple judgement calls about `<script src>` execution that we need to make. I'd like opinions from @jakearchibald and @tunetheweb as well as @zcorpan and others:)

1. when does the `close()` promise resolve

Currently it resolves after inline scripts are executed, but does not block on remote scripts (either parser-blocking or `defer`/`module`).

We can either:
(a) keep that
(b) block the promise on classic parser-blocking scripts only (equivalent to `document.readyState === "interactive"`)
(c) block on all defer/module scripts (equivalent to `DOMContentLoaded`)This might create deadlocks where a top-level await is blocked on the `write`, we'd have to account for that.

Note that the `close` promise is what drives `pipeTo` completion etc as well.

In (b) and (c) we'd have to error the stream if fetching these scripts fail and deal with some re-entrancy situations.

Currently thinking that (b) is a sweet spot.

2. What happens on a stream `abort` when the parser has un-processed tokens

Right now it would abort after processing those tokens.
Doing something else would create situations where tokens that were already supposedly inserted successfully are not in fact parsed.

I think this behavior is consistent enough, and avoids deadlocky situations with parser-blocking script, `document.write()` and `abort()`.

For 1, (b) SGTM. I think we shouldn't do (a) because it seems surprising to not have the whole DOM at `close` and I think could lead to more bugs (e.g. with cached scripts it works fine during development but for users it breaks).

Yeah I think  agree, for the same reasons.

> In (b) and (c) we'd have to error the stream if fetching these scripts fail and deal with some re-entrancy situations.

I'm not sure I agree with this. For normal parsing of the HTML document we wouldn't error if we have bad HTML or invalid scripts, but just error those and carry on. The robustness of HTML to bad authoring (or failed subresources) is a feature not a bug!

For 2. The current logic seems fine.

> > In (b) and (c) we'd have to error the stream if fetching these scripts fail and deal with some re-entrancy situations.
> 
> I'm not sure I agree with this. For normal parsing of the HTML document we wouldn't error if we have bad HTML or invalid scripts, but just error those and carry on. The robustness of HTML to bad authoring (or failed subresources) is a feature not a bug!

Sorry, my comment about that was wrong.

Reviewed at `c471a4f`, with web-platform-tests/wpt#61748 at `40837d5`. The Build check passes. Line numbers are for `source` at `c471a4f`; links go to the PR diff, and lines outside it are marked "unchanged". I traced write/close/abort re-entrancy, the pause and resume around parser-blocking scripts, *prepare the script element* (including the #13080 async behavior for `createContextualFragment()` and `setHTMLUnsafe()`), and the Trusted Types and Streams calls, and they look right. All 18 IDL members have matching method steps, and `[CEReactions]` is on exactly the methods that mutate synchronously.

**Blockers**

- **Nodes dropped after the reference node is displaced still have side effects, and the loss isn't reported.** If the reference node is moved or removed by script that runs during parsing (a streamed script, a custom element reaction, or the parser-blocking script the parser was waiting on), the rest of that run is still parsed, but nodes that would be inserted before the reference node are dropped:
  - *create an element for a token* redirects `intendedParent` to the target ([source:146977](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR146977)), so the element is created in the live document. *insert an element at the adjusted insertion location* then drops it ([source:147280](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR147280)), but it's still pushed onto the stack of open elements and its descendants are built inside it. So image and media fetches can start, and custom element constructors run (through the upgrade queued at creation), for markup that never reaches the DOM.
  - The sanitizing parser goes out of its way to keep markup that doesn't reach the DOM inert: no speculative fetches while sanitizing (`source:146960`, unchanged), removed elements created in the appropriate template contents owner document so they "do not invoke side effects such as loading images" ([source:147013](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR147013)), and a null registry so no constructor runs (`source:147032`, unchanged). Dropped nodes get none of that, so the safe methods have effects outside their sanitized result whenever the config allows images, media, or custom elements (the built-in default allows none of them). The Unsafe methods behave the same way.
  - The loss is silent and timing-dependent. The write resolves and so does `close()` ([WPT E1](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/40837d587f359bcc13c34ca1239d8c2cc0ff5021/domparsing/stream-insertion-logic.html#L235-L267)); an error is only reported if another write follows, and moving the node back lets the stream carry on ([WPT E2](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/40837d587f359bcc13c34ca1239d8c2cc0ff5021/domparsing/stream-insertion-logic.html#L327-L349)). For example, take `loading.streamBeforeHTMLUnsafe({runScripts: true})` with markup that ends in `<script>loading.remove()</script>` followed by more content. If the trailing content arrives in the same chunk, it's silently dropped; if it arrives later, `pipeTo()` rejects. If the parser was waiting on a `<script src>` near the end, `close()` has often already been called, so whatever follows that script and would go before `loading` disappears while `close()` succeeds.
  - Chromium does the same: `HTMLConstructionSite::CreateElement()` takes its document from `OwnerDocumentForCurrentNode()`, which resolves to the target's document, and `Insert()` returns early when `InsertionLocation::IsValid()` fails. So this needs a decision in the spec rather than an implementation fix.
  - Consider checking when the element is created, since checking at insertion is too late: in *create an element for a token*, if the redirect's reference child is no longer a child of its target parent, create the element in the appropriate template contents owner document with a null registry, like an element the sanitizer removes, so its whole subtree stays inert. Also consider erroring the stream at that point (Streams' "error a WritableStream") and rejecting a pending *fragment parser close promise*, which *abort a parser* doesn't settle today. WPT E1 and E2 would need to change. A test like the existing [removeElements one](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/40837d587f359bcc13c34ca1239d8c2cc0ff5021/domparsing/stream-insertion-logic.html#L300-L325), but with a config that keeps `img` and a custom element, would cover the side effects.

**Suggestions**

- PR description (commit message):
  - It says `isStream` is set to true; the Trusted Types parameter is `throwIfMissing`.
  - It says the *script target document* is "the redirected target's node document", but *initialize an HTML fragment parser* uses the context element's node document ([source:153054](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR153054)). They differ for `template`.
  - Consider listing the normative changes to existing APIs:
    - *the end* now returns early for fragment parsers. On main it spins the event loop unconditionally, even for `innerHTML`.
    - Elements whose intended parent is the root are now created directly in the fragment's node document, not in the inert document and then adopted.
    - Fragment parsers that don't run scripts no longer process SVG `script` ([source:151589](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR151589)), although the description calls SVG `script` processing (#902) out of scope.
    - Elements the sanitizer removes or replaces with their children are now created in the appropriate template contents owner document, also for `parseHTML()`.
  - Consider condensing it; it's long for a commit message.
  - The MDN box is ticked, but the issue hasn't been filed yet.
- *create an element for a token* note ([source:146982](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR146982)): it says "When streaming HTML", but the redirect changes which document elements are created in for all fragment parsing. Consider rewording.
- Microtask timing between streamed scripts depends on what drives the parser. During a write the JavaScript execution context stack is never empty (the write runs under `writer.write()` or a Streams reaction), so neither the `</script>` checkpoint (`source:150156`, unchanged) nor "clean up after running script" runs microtasks between scripts. In the task that resumes after a parser-blocking script, both do. So `<script>queueMicrotask(…)</script><script>…</script>` can order differently depending on network timing. Consider at least documenting this.
- Intro ([source:127264](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127264)): `document.write()` from a streamed inline script implies `document.open()` whenever the live document has no insertion point, which includes while it's still loading, not only after it has finished parsing. Consider rewording.
- Note in the *in head* `script` steps ([source:148075](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR148075)): "document.write() calls … will execute in-line" isn't true for streamed scripts, which write to the live document. Consider saying it applies to a document's own parser.
- The *script-created parser* dfn (`source:126038`, unchanged) still describes only `document.open()` and `document.close()`, but the streaming parser is now also script-created ([source:128028](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR128028)). Consider updating it the way the "EOF" paragraph was.
- XSLT guidance (`source:69472`, unchanged): the cross-document check moved from *parser document* to *intended document*, so XSLT-created scripts now also need an intended document to keep that check. Consider updating the bullet.
- New parser state ([source:144031](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR144031)): consider a sentence each for *script target document*, *fragment parser running*, *aborted*, *fragment parser abort requested*, and *fragment parser close promise*, especially *script target document*, which decides whether scripts may run.
- *stream HTML* ([source:127977](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127977)) takes a boolean `safe` where its siblings take a *fragment parser mode*, and derives `runScripts` differently from *fragment parsing algorithm steps*. Consider aligning them.
- Domintro ([source:127349](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127349), [source:127380](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127380), and siblings): streams don't "reject" (writing rejects, or the stream errors); "no longer a child of its parent" can't happen as written ("of node's original parent"); "at the time of calling the method" is awkwardly placed; and "executed as they are parsed" only holds for connected targets.
- *XML fragment parsing algorithm* (`source:153548`, unchanged) still computes `context` inline, linked to a dfn that now reads `contextElement`. Consider using *parser context element* there too.
- Intro ([source:127289](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127289)): the `blocking="render"` sentence only applies to `defer` and module scripts when the stream is never closed (parser-blocking scripts are unblocked when they run), and only before the document has a body. Consider making that explicit.

**Nits**

- Intro ([source:127251](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127251)): `setHTML()` never runs scripts; compare with `setHTMLUnsafe()` instead.
- *parent for HTML streaming* note ([source:127965](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127965)): only `beforeHTML()`, `afterHTML()`, `replaceWithHTML()`, and their Unsafe versions do nothing without a parent, and the streaming methods aren't "HTML insertion methods" under that dfn.
- *abortAlgorithm* note ([source:128131](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR128131)): the last sentence reads like a non sequitur.
- Streams dependency ([source:2822](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR2822)): lowercase "set up", like the other entries.
- [source:128136](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR128136): Streams' own convention is "with writeAlgorithm set to writeAlgorithm, …".
- [source:127983](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR127983), [source:128401](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR128401), [source:153031](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR153031): the "Assert: … is non-null" is redundant, since *parser context element* never returns null.
- *adjusted insertion location* ([source:147180](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR147180)): "Return the parser's insertion target redirection map[targetParent]" would do; "target container" ([source:147184](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR147184)) isn't a defined term; [source:147194](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR147194) wraps early.
- [source:153005](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes/c471a4f9cab103fe6e3446390278d3200ac9d9d6#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR153005): "disconnected `DocumentFragment`" → one whose host is null.
